title: GlycanPUG: WURCS-Based Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Structurally Ambiguous Glycans
zh_title: GlycanPUG：面向结构不确定聚糖的WURCS异质图预训练
summary: 提出基于WURCS 2.0的不确定性感知异质图预训练模型GlycanPUG，用加权边保留聚糖结构歧义，以弥补IUPAC确定性流程仅处理43.1%队列的局限。
key_points: 以加权边和不确定性属性表示候选连接
4层异质图神经网络含节点预增强模块
IUPAC流程仅覆盖GlyCosmos队列43.1%
reason: 新方法预印本，摘要未见充分对比与验证，属增量档
abstract: Background: Glycans orchestrate diverse biological processes, yet they remain underrepresented in computational biology compared to proteins and nucleic acids. Although WURCS 2.0 provides a machine-readable structural representation that preserves uncertainty, the evaluated IUPAC-based deterministic workflow processes 43.1% of the GlyCosmos-derived cohort examined here, motivating approaches that retain structural ambiguity. Methods: To overcome this limitation, GlycanPUG (Probabilistic Uncertainty-aware Graph) was introduced as a pretrained graph model for glycan representation learning. By leveraging WURCS 2.0, GlycanPUG represents candidate linkages and substituent attachments using weighted edges and uncertainty attributes within a heterogeneous graph framework. A 4-layer Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with a dedicated node pre-enhancement module aggregates edge features weighted by the assigned edge weights, enabling representation of supported structurally ambiguous glycans without selecting a single resolved structure. The model is pretrained on a preprocessed subset of the GlyTouCan1 repository, which contained 253,596 entries before filtering. After excluding entries linked to downstream tasks and applying sequential structural filtering, 167,020 samples remained and were used for pretraining. Pretraining comprised nine self-supervised tasks. Results: Benchmarking on the GlycanML dataset demonstrates that GlycanPUG shows competitive performance relative to GlycanGT across multi-label taxonomy classification and binary immunogenicity prediction. Crucially, on datasets natively containing structural uncertainties (GlyCosmos, GlyConnect), GlycanPUG effectively processes additional structurally ambiguous entries, achieving 83.5% processable coverage across all glycans from all biological sources in GlyCosmos, with taxonomic classification performance (e.g., mean macro F1 of 0.7376 for Domain). Ablation of the node pre-enhancement module reduces macro F1, and post-hoc analysis identifies rank-dependent associations between structural uncertainty and prediction errors. All results reported above are averaged over ten independent random seeds (1-10). Conclusions: GlycanPUG broadens the set of glycans that can be represented while retaining supported structural ambiguities.
zh_abstract: 【背景】聚糖调控多种生物学过程，但与蛋白质和核酸相比，其在计算生物学中的代表性仍然不足。尽管 WURCS 2.0 提供了一种可保留不确定性的机器可读结构表示，但所评估的基于 IUPAC 的确定性工作流程仅能处理此处所检视的源自 GlyCosmos 的队列的 43.1%，这促使人们寻求能够保留结构模糊性的方法。【方法】为克服这一局限，引入了 GlycanPUG（Probabilistic Uncertainty-aware Graph，概率性不确定性感知图），作为用于聚糖表征学习的预训练图模型。GlycanPUG 借助 WURCS 2.0，在异质图框架内使用加权边和不确定性属性来表示候选连接和取代基连接。一个带有专用节点预增强模块的 4 层异质图神经网络（Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network）按所分配的边权重聚合边特征，从而能够表示受支持的结构模糊聚糖，而无需选择单一的确定结构。该模型在 GlyTouCan1 数据库经预处理的子集上进行预训练，该子集在过滤前包含 253,596 个条目。在排除与下游任务相关的条目并进行连续结构过滤后，剩余 167,020 个样本用于预训练。预训练包含九项自监督任务。【结果】在 GlycanML 数据集上的基准测试表明，在多标签分类学分类和二元免疫原性预测方面，GlycanPUG 相对于 GlycanGT 表现出具有竞争力的性能。关键的是，在天然含有结构不确定性的数据集（GlyCosmos、GlyConnect）上，GlycanPUG 能有效处理更多结构模糊的条目，在 GlyCosmos 中来自所有生物来源的全部聚糖上实现了 83.5% 的可处理覆盖率，并具有分类学分类性能（例如，Domain 的平均宏 F1 为 0.7376）。去除节点预增强模块会降低宏 F1，事后分析发现结构不确定性与预测错误之间存在依赖于排名的关联。上述所有结果均为十个独立随机种子（1-10）的平均值。【结论】GlycanPUG 在保留受支持的结构模糊性的同时，拓宽了可被表示的聚糖范围。

title: A Two-Stage YOLO-Swin Transformer Pipeline for Cross-Dataset White Blood Cell Classification
zh_title: 两阶段YOLO-Swin流程用于跨数据集白细胞分类
summary: YOLO11检测裁剪加Swin-B九类分类，在五个公开数据集上训练，并以未参与训练的WBCBench2026公开基准做外部评估。
key_points: 第一阶段YOLO11检测并保留背景裁剪
第二阶段Swin-B进行九类分类
色彩增强与类别加权应对染色和不平衡
reason: 有外部基准评估但方法常规，属增量档
abstract: Background: White blood cell (WBC) classification across datasets is challenged by differences in staining, image context, and class distributions. Methods: We developed a two-stage YOLO11-Swin Transformer pipeline. In the first stage, WBC detection and context-preserving cropping, a YOLO11 detector finds the leukocyte in each uncropped image and produces a cell-focused crop that retains the surrounding background. In the second stage, WBC classification, a Swin Transformer (Swin-B) assigns the crop to one of nine cell types. The classifier was trained on detector-cropped cells from five public datasets, so the first stage supplies the same kind of input at test time; morphology-preserving color augmentation addressed staining variation, and class-weighted cross-entropy addressed class imbalance. WBCBench2026, a public benchmark not used for training, served for external evaluation in seven harmonized classes, scored by macro-F1 (the mean of per-class F1). Further analyses removed the first stage or masked the background, compared classifier backbones, held out each training dataset (leave-one-dataset-out, LODO), and tested a second split (Phase-2) with about 60% synthetically degraded images. Results: The full pipeline reached an external macro-F1 of 0.879{+/-}0.006 on 8,080 benchmark images. With uncropped images as input, the same crop-trained classifier reached 0.627{+/-}0.039, and crops that kept the surrounding background outperformed background-masked crops (0.867 versus 0.760). With identical detector-cropped input, Swin-B outperformed convolutional baselines (0.863 versus 0.718-0.813), and its advantage over ResNet50 persisted across three training configurations. In LODO, macro-F1 on the held-out dataset ranged from 0.59 to 0.91, revealing source-specific variation not fully covered by the remaining datasets. On Phase-2, macro-F1 was 0.769{+/-}0.002. Two hematologists independently reviewed all 205 blast- or promyelocyte-related model-benchmark disagreements and gave the same verdict on 73 crops (35.6%): 21 model right, 43 model wrong, 9 ambiguous. Conclusions: The proposed two-stage pipeline achieved strong cross-dataset WBC classification performance. Context-preserving cropping was essential for the crop-trained classifier, and the LODO findings support representing the same classes across diverse sources when developing robust WBC classifiers.
zh_abstract: 【背景】不同数据集之间的白细胞（WBC）分类面临染色、图像背景和类别分布差异的挑战。【方法】我们开发了一个两阶段的 YOLO11-Swin Transformer 流程。第一阶段为白细胞检测及保留背景的裁剪：YOLO11 检测器在每幅未裁剪图像中找到白细胞，并生成以细胞为中心、保留周围背景的裁剪图。第二阶段为白细胞分类：Swin Transformer（Swin-B）将裁剪图归入九种细胞类型之一。分类器在来自五个公开数据集的、经检测器裁剪的细胞上训练，因此第一阶段在测试时提供同类输入；保留形态的颜色增强用于应对染色差异，类别加权交叉熵用于应对类别不平衡。WBCBench2026 是未用于训练的公开基准，用于在七个统一后的类别上进行外部评估，以宏平均 F1（各类别 F1 的均值）评分。进一步的分析包括：去除第一阶段或遮蔽背景、比较分类器骨干网络、逐一留出每个训练数据集（留一数据集法，LODO），以及检验约 60% 图像经合成退化的第二种划分（Phase-2）。【结果】完整流程在 8,080 幅基准图像上的外部宏平均 F1 为 0.879±0.006。以未裁剪图像作为输入时，同一经裁剪图训练的分类器为 0.627±0.039；保留周围背景的裁剪图优于背景被遮蔽的裁剪图（0.867 对 0.760）。在相同的检测器裁剪输入下，Swin-B 优于卷积基线（0.863 对 0.718–0.813），且其相对于 ResNet50 的优势在三种训练配置下均持续存在。在 LODO 中，留出数据集上的宏平均 F1 为 0.59 至 0.91，显示出其余数据集未能完全覆盖的来源特异性差异。在 Phase-2 上，宏平均 F1 为 0.769±0.002。两名血液科医师独立复核了全部 205 例与原始细胞或早幼粒细胞相关的模型与基准不一致病例，对 73 个裁剪图（35.6%）给出相同判定：模型正确 21 个，模型错误 43 个，存在歧义 9 个。【结论】所提出的两阶段流程在跨数据集白细胞分类中取得了良好性能。对于经裁剪图训练的分类器，保留背景的裁剪至关重要；LODO 结果支持在开发稳健的白细胞分类器时，使相同类别由多样化来源共同代表。

title: Evaluating Prominent Machine Translation Models for Kinyarwanda to English for Patient-Provider Conversations
zh_title: 卢旺达语到英语医患对话的机器翻译模型评估
summary: 预印本用600段WelTel平台医患对话，比较GPT-5、Gemini、Google Translate、NLLB-200等六个系统，结合自动指标和三位专业译者评分。
key_points: 评估六个机器翻译系统
600段卢旺达医患对话参考语料
自动指标与人工0–100评分结合
reason: 低资源语言评估有价值，但摘要缺结果，规模有限
abstract: Background Linguistic barriers between patients and providers cause diagnostic error, poor adherence, and adverse events, and disproportionately affect speakers of low-resource languages. Kinyarwanda, spoken by more than 20 million people, has a small digital footprint, and the quality of off-the-shelf machine translation (MT) for its clinical dialogue is poorly documented. Methods We evaluated six MT systems (GPT-5, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Azure Translate, Google Translate, and NLLB-200) for Kinyarwanda-to-English patient-provider conversations. Using a professional reference corpus of 600 conversations, stratified across three pandemic periods and collected in Rwanda via the WelTel platform, we assessed automated metrics (semantic similarity, BLEU, chrF, and translation edit rate [TER]) and 0-100 quality ratings from three professional Kinyarwanda-English translators, with reliability quantified by intraclass correlation (ICC). De-identified secondary data were approved by UBC (H20-01031) and the Rwanda National Ethics Committee (100/RNEC/2020). Findings On the full 600-conversation cohort, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash had closely clustered semantic similarity (0.877, 0.874, 0.873), well above Azure Translate (0.809) and NLLB-200 (0.754); Gemini 2.5 Flash led on BLEU (43.13) and the lowest TER (68.15). Translators ranked GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash highest (means 81.55 and 81.51), then GPT-4o-mini (72.67), Azure Translate (55.16), and NLLB-200 (39.05); average-rater reliability was moderate (ICC 0.594, rising to 0.701 on a balanced 85-conversation subset). Automated n-gram metrics understated the quality gap human raters perceived between large language models and conventional systems. Interpretation GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash are the strongest off-the-shelf systems for Kinyarwanda-English clinical translation and primary choices for human-in-the-loop use, with GPT-4o-mini a cost-efficient alternative. NLLB-200 underperformed, showing that models built for low-resource languages are not automatically suited to specialised clinical domains without fine-tuning. Human evaluation should be prioritised over automated metrics alone when comparing LLM-based translation.
zh_abstract:
【背景】患者与医疗提供者之间的语言障碍会导致诊断错误、依从性差和不良事件，并对低资源语言使用者造成不成比例的影响。卢旺达语（Kinyarwanda）使用者逾 2000 万人，但其数字资源很少，现成机器翻译（MT）对其临床对话的翻译质量也缺乏充分记录。
【方法】我们评估了六个 MT 系统（GPT-5、GPT-4o-mini、Gemini 2.5 Flash、Azure Translate、Google Translate 和 NLLB-200）在卢旺达语到英语的医患对话翻译中的表现。我们使用通过 WelTel 平台在卢旺达收集、按三个疫情时期分层的 600 段对话的专业参考语料库，评估了自动指标（语义相似度、BLEU、chrF 和翻译编辑率 [TER]）以及三名卢旺达语-英语专业译员给出的 0-100 质量评分，并以组内相关系数（ICC）量化可靠性。去标识化的二次数据已获 UBC（H20-01031）和卢旺达国家伦理委员会（100/RNEC/2020）批准。
【结果】在完整的 600 段对话队列中，GPT-4o-mini、GPT-5 和 Gemini 2.5 Flash 的语义相似度非常接近（0.877、0.874、0.873），明显高于 Azure Translate（0.809）和 NLLB-200（0.754）；Gemini 2.5 Flash 的 BLEU 最高（43.13），TER 最低（68.15）。译员将 GPT-5 和 Gemini 2.5 Flash 评为最高（均值 81.55 和 81.51），其后依次为 GPT-4o-mini（72.67）、Azure Translate（55.16）和 NLLB-200（39.05）；评分者平均可靠性为中等（ICC 0.594，在均衡的 85 段对话子集上升至 0.701）。自动 n-gram 指标低估了人工评分者所感知到的大语言模型与传统系统之间的质量差距。
【结论】GPT-5 和 Gemini 2.5 Flash 是卢旺达语-英语临床翻译中最强的现成系统，是人在回路使用的首选，GPT-4o-mini 是具成本效益的替代选择。NLLB-200 表现欠佳，表明为低资源语言构建的模型若未经微调，并不自然适用于专业临床领域。在比较基于大语言模型的翻译时，应优先采用人工评估，而不是仅依赖自动指标。

abstract: Objectives: This study developed machine learning (ML) to predict 90-day preventable admissions in CKD patients while evaluating racial disparities in model performance. Materials and Methods: Study population included CKD patients (above 18 years) with hospital encounters in Maryland (2016-2023). Logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, and k-nearest neighbors (KNN) models were used to predict 90-day preventable admissions after a CKD outpatient visit. Data used in this study was extracted from Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project (HCUP). Results: 28,214 unique patients were included, of whom 3974 (14%) experienced a subsequent preventable admission. LR achieved comparable performance with RF and XGBoost (AuROC 0.784 - 0.788, AuPRC 0.397 - 0.416), outperforming KNN (AuROC 0.753, AuPRC 0.342). All models performed marginally better in the Black population (AuROC 0.773 - 0.807, AuPRC 0.369 - 0.467) than in the white population (AuROC 0.738 - 0.776, AuPRC 0.329 - 0.394). The false negative rates (FNR) in the white population were higher across different models (Black: 0.236 - 0.33, white: 0.297 - 0.377). Discussion: Our results suggest that LR can achieve comparable prediction performances than tree-based ML algorithms. Hospital utilization and congestive heart failure are among the most important predictors across models. Further analyses on prediction bias revealed that FNRs are more significant in white patients, which can be due to their overall lower utilization. Conclusions: This study demonstrated a pipeline to develop ML models predicting preventable admissions while revealing existing racial biases. These findings can inform ambulatory settings on how to reduce preventable admissions among CKD patients.

abstract: [Frontiers in public health] With the deep integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into public health and clinical care, challenges including dynamic algorithm iteration, data security risks, and ambiguous liability allocation pose multifaceted threats to traditional regulatory frameworks. Among these challenges, this study focuses specifically on the tension between static pre-market approval and the continuous iteration of AI-enabled medical systems. Globally, the European Union (EU), the United States (US), and Japan have developed distinct regulatory models that offer valuable lessons for China. This paper conducts a comparative analysis of medical AI regulatory logics and institutional practices across jurisdictions, with particular attention to algorithm modification, lifecycle oversight, and continuous post-market evaluation. Building on international experience, we propose an optimized institutional pathway for China that centers on differentiated algorithm-change control, continuous lifecycle evaluation, and risk-based regulatory adjustment, while treating liability allocation, risk classification, and data governance as supporting dimensions. This framework provides theoretical support and practical guidance for improving China's medical AI regulatory system, promoting standardized technology development, and supporting the orderly development of public health services in the digital health era.

abstract: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Continuous monitoring, timely intervention, and personalized long-term management are necessary for chronic diseases. Conventional healthcare systems often fail to assess patients' health status in real time. Cloud-edge-device collaborative computing combines Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, edge computing, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI) to enable distributed processing and remote healthcare delivery. This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence on the application of cloud-edge-device collaborative computing in the management of chronic diseases. The Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines were used in this scoping review. PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, Google Scholar, and selected grey literature sources were searched from database inception to 1 July 2026, with results limited to studies published from 2000 onward. Original cloud-edge-device collaborative computing studies focused on chronic disease management were included, and data were analyzed narratively. Ten studies, including experimental implementations, system development studies, conceptual frameworks, and one randomized controlled trial published between 2015 and 2025, were included. Cloud-edge-device architectures were applied in the management of diabetes (n = 5), monitoring of cardiovascular disease (n = 1), management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD; n = 1), and multi-disease/multi-morbidity applications (n = 3). IoMT devices continuously obtained physiological data, while edge/fog layers processed local data, reduced latency, and made real-time decisions. Cloud platforms stored and analyzed large-scale data and trained the models. Artificial intelligence methods, especially machine-learning algorithms, predicted and assessed disease risks. However, only one study was a clinical trial involving patients; most studies used benchmark datasets, volunteers, or simulations, meaning real-world clinical validation remains limited. Cloud-edge-device collaborative computing has been used to integrate distributed computing, IoMT, and AI for chronic disease management, but current evidence is mainly technical, and its clinical benefits remain largely unestablished.

abstract: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys. Therefore, patient journeys are important assets to investigate how care is being provided, and how health systems can be designed to better suit the needs of patients. While there is initial work on patient journeys from a process mining perspective with traditional case notions, object-centric process mining techniques have yet to be covered. abstract: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.

abstract: Bioconductor provides standardized data structures and statistical methods for high-throughput genomic analysis in R, whereas Python has become a primary environment for machine learning, image analysis, and general-purpose data science. Combining tools across both ecosystems often requires ad-hoc file conversions or embedded language runtimes that can lose metadata, introduce maintenance overhead, or lead to subtle differences in downstream results. Here, we present BiocPy, a collection of Python packages that support cross-language genomic workflows through three complementary layers: (1) native Python implementations of Bioconductor's core data structures; (2) lossless data exchange via direct reading and writing of serialized R (.rds) objects and the language-neutral ArtifactDB format for persistent, multi-stage pipelines; and (3) a cross-platform method development paradigm built on shared C++ libraries wrapped across R, Python, and WebAssembly to support identical statistical analyses across environments. All packages in the BiocPy ecosystem are published to the Python Package Index (PyPI) with source code hosted at [https://github.com/BiocPy].
